summary:
NOT RUN IN THE REAL GAME: nothing here was run in the real client, against a server or through scripts/e2e.mjs (ports 8420/8421 were in use by the browser-test engineer; I never touched them or .data). Everything was seen on the dev page, scene 'surface' with universe=16&base=0, which is the moon the owner named (Hellear IV a, radius 1,057 km, 0.60 m/s^2, day 3.81 d, base Ezis Ground), with the terrain part on unless a line says 'plain'.

THIS WAS A RESUMED TASK. An earlier session of this role had already written the model, the four pads, the registration, the ground structures, a landing light, the dust and new belly numbers (committed 06:26 to 07:11, no report). I audited all of it, kept what held, and changed what failed:
1. LANDING LIGHT WAS NOT DONE: on bare ground at night it was invisible (pool at a fifth of sunlight is crushed to black by the tone curve; at 30 m nothing, landed nothing). Redesigned as a regulated wide flood; a night approach can now be flown by eye from about 250 m down. Weak spots that remain: a landed ship lights only a patch under its nose and the ground around stays black; from the cockpit the dashboard hides most of the pool (faint ground only with the nose pitched 15 degrees down); a large hull flying low covers most of its own pool in the chase view.
2. BELLY DEVIATES FROM 'LOWEST POINT' FOR TWO HULLS (decision of the earlier session, kept, see behaviour): Drover and Bulwark stand on the underside of the hull, not on their antenna (0.88 m) and keel blade (1.65 m), which stand in the ground. I corrected the Bulwark from 2.9 to 2.85 (it floated 5 cm). This changes the rules fingerprint once more.
3. GLARE: seen against a low sun the apron of the base was a white disc and each pad a white disc with its number gone. Regolith materials are now matte and pad plates and paint keep a tenth of the grazing sheen. To make up for the lost sheen at night I raised the floodlights from 95 to 150.
4. The lamp was first tuned on dark regolith only; on bright ice the pool was near white (205 of 255). It is now regulated by the reflectance of the ground under the ship (87 on ice, 63 on the test moon at 30 m).
5. The point of light of the lamp hung up to 2 m below the nose of the big hulls; it now sits on the hull (ray cast per model).

What is true now: base_ground.glb exists (four numbered lift-platform pads, compound, tower, 77 lamps), is registered in STRUCTURES and on every generated base, with the pads as data on the structure; ground bases are drawn on their pad, turned with the body, sunlit by day and floodlit at night; hull belly values are measured; landing lamps, dust, bursts and the quiet landed ship work on the dev page. Final state: tsc clean for all three packages, 40 test files, 606 passed plus 2 expected fail, client builds into a scratch directory with models/base_ground.glb in it. At 12:20:44 the tree had one uncommitted file of mine (a comment in objects/landing.ts); the checkpoint job is running (last commit 4697573 at 12:17:51).

Not mine and not done: hud=1 and the two HUD screenshots (addressed to the terrain engineer; hud=1 already exists in dev/local.ts, not by me).
behaviour:
BELLY (packages/shared/src/catalog.ts), metres from origin down. Columns: old guess 0.3 r / lowest point of the GLB / underside by the rule 'lowest height where the cut through the model is at least 1 m wide and 1 m long' / value in the catalog.
wisp 2.7 / 0.942 / 0.939 / 0.94
lancet 3.0 / 1.354 / 1.341 / 1.35
drover 7.2 / 4.309 / 3.429 / 3.43
delver 5.1 / 3.725 / 3.707 / 3.73
wayfarer 4.8 / 2.915 / 2.894 / 2.92
bulwark 7.8 / 4.500 / 2.851 / 2.85 (the earlier session had 2.9)
So four hulls stand on their lowest point; Drover and Bulwark on the hull underside. What hangs below: Drover a whip antenna 7 x 9 cm thick, 0.88 m long, 13 m ahead of the origin; Bulwark a keel blade 0.5 m wide, 7 m long, 1.65 m deep, aft.

BASE MODEL (assets/blender/structures/base_ground.py, packages/client/public/models/base_ground.glb). 22,030 triangles, 29,677 vertices, 1,085 kB. Origin = middle of the compound at ground level, +Y up, north -Z. Compound inside r 89.6 m (collider r 90, 0..40 m), tower and mast to 107.9 m inside r 10.8 (collider r 14, 40..110 m), habitat hulls reach 3.3 m below ground under their berms. Apron disc r 235 m (bound 250, terrain flat to 400). Pads 1..4 clockwise from north at (0,0,-170), (170,0,0), (0,0,170), (-170,0,0), radius 40: lift plate r 34, seam to 34.6, hazard ring to 37.6, collar to 40, touchdown circle r 20, number 14 m tall with its top toward the compound, 16 edge lights at 41.4 m. Nothing stands inside a 40 m disc (highest thing there: paint at 0.099 m); edge lights (0.5 m), a service pit (1 m, 43 m from the pad centre on the hub side) and pipes are outside it and have no collider. Lamps as empties light_0..76: 8 flood (two masts per pad, 36 m up), 1 beacon, 1 work, 3 door, 64 edge. Colliders unchanged from the first core engineer's shape.

GROUND STRUCTURES (objects/structures.ts). A site with `ground` is drawn at view.sites[i].rel with orientation surface.rot x groundSiteRotation(site) (bodyRotation when the camera is near another body). Not drawn when its pad is more than 300 m below the horizon of the smooth body, unless the camera is within 20 km. Model above 2 px projected bound radius, a point of light below 7 px. Day factor = smoothstep of the sine of the sun's height at the base between -0.02 and 0.06; floodlight glass, flood and work lamps follow night = 1 - day; edge lights (blue-white), beacon (red, 1 s on, 1 s off) and door lamps burn always; edge lights are drawn within 9 km. Real lights: four spot lights (one per pad, from the middle of its two masts to the pad centre, cone 0.56 rad, reach 280 m, strength 150, falling with distance not its square) and one point light over the compound (80, reach 150 m), on for the nearest base within 5 km, full strength within 3.75 km, off at quality 0. The three flat layers ground, pads, marks are drawn with polygon offset units -4, -8, -12. Everything named rock_* is tinted to the ground reflectance at the site, lit like the terrain (back-scatter term) and has no specular reflection at all; pad plates, paint and the other non-emissive parts of the flat layers keep a grazing reflectance of at most 0.12.

LANDING LIGHT (objects/landing.ts, numbers in render/local/util.ts). On below 500 m (lowest point of the hull above ground), full from 440 m down; Normal and Landed only. Own ship: one SpotLight, colour 0xfff3df, strength falling with distance (decay 1), nothing lit beyond 1,200 m, cone half angle 1.08 rad with the outer half fading, leaning 0.52 rad from straight down toward the nose, so the cone ends at the level of the lamp. It leaves the ship 0.3 m below the belly plane, 0.4 hull radii ahead of the origin. Strength = pool x clamp(height + 0.3, 1.5, 160) x switch level x (0.1 + 0.9 x (1 - sunlight)), pool = clamp(0.5 / reflectance of the ground under the ship, 0.5, 5): about 4.5 on the test moon, 0.7 on bright ice. Above 160 m the pool thins with 1/height. Other ships: a warm point of light on the hull under the nose, level by their height above ground within 30 km, 0.45 when landed (EntityFlag.Landed); no real light.

DUST (fx/regolith.ts, the earlier session's, unchanged except how the lamp lights it). Thrust is read from the ship's acceleration plus gravity; exhaust within 40 m of the ground raises grains: up to 520 per second for the own ship at 70 kN and above, 160 for other ships within 900 m; they leave at 0.03 to 0.3 rad above the surface at up to 9 + 34 x strength m/s, fly ballistic arcs under the body's gravity, at most 9 s, and are gone when the arc returns to the ground; at most 4,200 grains. The apron of a base gives 0.3 of the dust, a pad disc none. Bursts: own touchdown (sink + 0.4 x ground speed) x 1.6 when above 0.4; a 'hit' event within 0.8 m of the ground clamp(damage / 4, 2, 32); a shot that ends in the ground 2.5; a ship destroyed within 40 m of the ground 34. Dust is lit by the sun and, at night, by the own landing lamp with the same cone and falloff as the light.

LANDED SHIP (objects/craft.ts, the earlier session's). Own ship in mode Landed: engine glow at idle (3 %), no plume, no attitude jets, whatever the throttle; lamp on. Hovering under flight assist the downward jets burn in proportion to gravity over vertical thrust.

base_ground.glb nodes: base_ground_mesh (compound), ground, pads, marks (flat layers, bottom to top), empties pad_1..pad_4 at the pad centres, light_0..light_76 with extras p2_light (flood|edge|beacon|work|door) and p2_pad (1..4 or 0)

packages/client/src/render/local/util.ts LANDING_LIGHT_HEIGHT = 500, LAMP_HALF_ANGLE 1.08, LAMP_PENUMBRA 0.5, LAMP_FORWARD 0.52, LAMP_DROP 0.3, LAMP_FORE 0.4 - the landing lamp in numbers, shared by objects and fx

util.ts landingLampLevel(height): 0..1 and landingLampIntensity(height, level, sunlight, albedo): number - strength of the lamp for a light with decay 1; albedo is the reflectance of the ground under the ship

util.ts reflectance(r, g, b) - luminance of a linear colour; groundAlbedo(color, cls, tone, out) - ground reflectance in numbers, must follow terrain/shade.ts; sunVisibility(view, sunDir) - 0..1, how much of the sun reaches the camera past the body it is near

packages/client/src/render/local/objects/models.ts Model.chin: Vector3 | null - point on the hull underside below the nose where the landing lamp shows (ray cast at load), null for anything but a ship
packages/client/src/render/local/objects/landing.ts LandingLight (the own ship's spot light, .level 0..1) and GroundProbe (height of a camera-relative point above the terrain)
packages/client/src/render/local/objects/structures.ts FLOOD_INTENSITY 150, WORK_INTENSITY 80, FLOOD_RANGE 5000, DUSTY_SHEEN 0.12, FLAT_LAYERS - tuning of the base's lights and flat layers

done: Audit of the earlier session's work in my area: read every file, attributed it from its edit scripts in the scratchpad (shared structures/generate/types/bases.test/catalog/landing.test; client objects craft, index, landing, structures; fx regolith, index, core; util.ts), ran baseline checks (tsc clean, 605 passed + 2 expected fail before my first edit)

Item 1, model: base_ground.glb with compound, three bermed habitats, tank farm, shed with rover, radiators, dish, hopper, cargo, power bank, ring main and pipe runs, eight floodlight masts, tower with mast; four numbered lift-platform pads per the owner's note, pad centres as data on the structure and as empties pad_1..pad_4; registered in STRUCTURES, on generated bases and in bases.test.ts (all by the earlier session; verified by me: generator dry run in Blender gives the same 22,030 triangles and box, verify_glb on the file reports ok with no problems, nothing stands on a pad)

Item 2, structures on the ground: stand on the pad with the helper's orientation, sunlit by day, floodlit at night (earlier session); this session: regolith materials made matte, grazing sheen of pad plates and paint capped at 0.12, floodlights 95 to 150

Item 3, belly: measured again from the six GLBs with my own script, three numbers per hull reported, Bulwark corrected 2.9 to 2.85, catalog comment rewritten to say exactly which rule each hull follows, test table updated

Item 4, landing lights: redesigned (wide flood leaning 30 degrees forward, falls with distance, regulated by height and by ground reflectance, range 1,200 m, nothing above lamp level so the own hull is not lit); numbers moved to util.ts so the dust uses the same lamp; lamp point of light mounted on the hull by a ray cast per model
Item 5, dust: kept the earlier session's effect; dust at night is now lit by the real cone of the lamp instead of a round pool under the ship
Item 6, landed ship: checked by day on bare ground and on a pad for Wisp, Drover and Bulwark; no change needed
assets/blender/README.md: base_ground added to the list and its conventions written down (layers, empties, lamp properties, driven materials)
Before and after comparison of the nine older dev scenes against a copy of the client at d4f7b22 (before this role's work), by eye and by frame time

Final checks: tsc x3 clean, vitest 40 files 606 passed + 2 expected fail, vite build into a scratch directory with models/base_ground.glb present; both dev servers I started stopped by PID, the node_modules junction of the comparison copy removed

The Drover's antenna and the Bulwark's keel blade stand in the ground of a landed ship; the ship models were not changed. The Drover's antenna is inside the lamp's cone edge and may show as a thin lit line under the nose at night; not looked at closely

No automated test covers the client render code of this task (landing light, dust, ground structures, lamp mount); none was added

The touchdown burst of the pilot's own ship was seen only through a fake descent on the dev page (a ship flown through the ground at 10 and 30 m/s); a real hard landing with the server's 'hit' event was not seen

The GLB was not exported again this session and assets/blender/previews/base_ground.png was not re-rendered; my Blender renders are scratch files. The dry run rebuilt the collection P2_base_ground in the running Blender, which is not saved
